title: Random-example and work bounds
statement: Let $n\ge 1$, let $d,Q$ be nonnegative integers, and let $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$. For any Boolean function on the sign cube and any outcome in the support of the program that uses the decision-tree-size influence bound with parameters $n,d,\varepsilon$, the number of random examples is at most $C(d+1,Q)(n+1)^{E(d+1,Q)}$, the number of membership queries is zero, and the charged work is at most $W(d+1,Q)(n+1)^{F(d+1,Q)}$, where $C,E,W,F$ are the specified learning-consequence constants and exponents for random examples and work, respectively. The bound assumes $1/(Q+1)\le\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: the target is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the outcome belongs to the support of the specified program's run-with-cost distribution
